title: Astronautics names D. Eyton Zelazo president
summary: Zelazo succeeds Robert Atac in the role.
body_markdown:
Astronautics Corporation of America, a Wisconsin-based aerospace and defense company, today announced that D. Eyton Zelazo has become president, succeeding Robert Atac.


“On behalf of Astronautics, I thank Bob Atac for his leadership as president,” said Dr. Ronald Zelazo, Astronautics’ chief executive officer and chairman of the board.


“During his tenure, the company expanded its product lines and technologies, including airborne displays, air-ground communications systems, aircraft cybersecurity tools, and integrated systems solutions. We wish Bob and his family all the best.”


As president, Eyton Zelazo will lead the company’s strategic growth, product and technology development, and overall management. He will report to Dr. Ronald Zelazo.


Eyton Zelazo brings to the role more than 20 years of experience at Astronautics where he has held positions of increasing responsibility, including in engineering, program management, and business development.


Since 2022, he has served in an executive leadership role as the director of Avionics Solutions, one of the company’s key business units serving major aerospace original equipment manufacturers and the United States military.


He has also served on the company’s board of directors since 2016.


“As a privately held company, Astronautics was founded more than 67 years ago with a commitment to provide innovative and advanced technology to the aviation industry,” Dr. Ronald Zelazo said. “Eyton is the right leader to guide Astronautics into its next phase of growth.”


“I’m honored to lead Astronautics at this pivotal time,” Eyton Zelazo said. “My focus will be on growing the business by expanding our products, strengthening customer relationships, and carrying forward the values that have made Astronautics a trusted aerospace and defense partner.”


Eyton Zelazo holds a master of business administration degree from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee; a bachelor of business administration degree in marketing, management, and human resources from the University of Wisconsin-Madison; a bachelor of science degree in electrical engineering technology from the Milwaukee School of Engineering; and an associate of applied science degree from Gateway Technical College in Wisconsin.


*This press release was prepared and distributed by Astronautics Corporation of America.*
